questions.explanation: Subsistence farming produces little or no surplus for sale, unlike commercial agriculture.

questions.text: The soil type that retains water best but is poorly drained is
questions.explanation: Clay particles are very fine, giving small pore spaces that hold water and slow drainage.

questions.text: The best soil for the cultivation of most arable crops is
questions.explanation: Loam balances sand, silt and clay, giving good drainage, aeration and nutrient retention.

questions.text: The nutrient element that promotes vegetative growth and gives leaves a deep green colour is
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is a constituent of chlorophyll and protein; its deficiency causes chlorosis and stunting.

questions.text: The practice of growing legumes in rotation with cereals improves soil fertility because legumes
options: fix atmospheric nitrogen through root nodules
questions.explanation: Rhizobium bacteria in the nodules convert atmospheric nitrogen into a form plants can use.

questions.text: Maize is best classified as
questions.explanation: Cereals are grasses grown for their edible grains; maize, rice, sorghum and millet belong here.

questions.text: The method of propagating cassava is by
questions.explanation: Mature stem cuttings of about 25 cm are planted at an angle or horizontally.

questions.text: A chemical used to control weeds is called
questions.explanation: Herbicides may be selective or non-selective, and contact or systemic in action.

questions.text: The gestation period of a cow is approximately
questions.explanation: A cow carries her calf for about 280 days, roughly nine months.

questions.text: Ruminant animals are able to digest cellulose because of
questions.explanation: Bacteria and protozoa in the rumen ferment cellulose into volatile fatty acids the animal can absorb.

questions.text: Newcastle disease is a viral disease that affects
questions.explanation: It causes high mortality in chickens and is controlled mainly by vaccination.

questions.text: The implement used for the primary tillage of land is the
questions.explanation: The plough cuts and inverts the soil first; the harrow then breaks the clods in secondary tillage.

questions.text: A major problem of agricultural marketing in Nigeria is
options: poor rural road networks and inadequate storage
questions.explanation: Bad roads and weak storage cause heavy post-harvest losses and depress farm-gate prices.

questions.text: The primary role of an agricultural extension officer is to
options: buy produce on behalf of government
questions.explanation: Extension links research to the farm, carrying improved techniques to the farmer and problems back to researchers.

questions.text: The system of farming in which crops and animals are raised on the same farm is
questions.explanation: Mixed farming lets animal manure fertilise crops while crop residues feed the animals.

questions.text: Growing two or more crops on the same piece of land at the same time is
questions.explanation: Mixed cropping spreads risk and makes fuller use of soil nutrients and sunlight.

questions.text: Soil pH is a measure of the
questions.explanation: Most crops do best between pH 6 and 7; liming raises pH on acid soils.

questions.text: Terracing is a soil conservation practice used mainly to
questions.explanation: Terraces break a long slope into level steps, slowing run-off and reducing soil loss.

questions.text: Cocoa, rubber and oil palm are best described as
questions.explanation: They occupy the land for many years and yield over long productive lives.

questions.text: The weevil that attacks stored grains is best controlled by
options: proper drying and fumigation of the store
questions.explanation: Low moisture content and fumigation of clean, airtight stores prevent weevil infestation.

questions.text: The male reproductive organ of a farm animal that produces spermatozoa is the
questions.explanation: The testis produces both spermatozoa and the hormone testosterone.

questions.text: Feed given to animals to supply energy is mainly rich in
questions.explanation: Maize, cassava and sorghum are energy concentrates; groundnut cake and fishmeal supply protein.

questions.text: Fish farming in constructed ponds is known as
questions.explanation: Aquaculture is the controlled rearing of aquatic organisms; apiculture is beekeeping.

questions.text: Afforestation refers to
options: planting trees where none grew before
questions.explanation: Afforestation establishes new forest; reforestation replants an area that was previously forested.

questions.text: Land, labour, capital and management in farming are collectively known as
options: farm inputs or factors of production
questions.explanation: These four resources must be combined efficiently for profitable farm production.

questions.text: The farm record that shows income and expenditure over a period is the
questions.explanation: Financial records are the basis for computing profit or loss and for obtaining credit.
